A.source: I don't like the new medication.

B.source: I like the new medication.

notes: Health. Default: affirmative, and possibly a request ('I would like my medication'), which also changes speech act.

A.source: The lift is working again.

B.source: The lift isn't working again.

notes: Transport/access. 'again' fits both (fixed again / broken again). Default: possibly negated (complaint frame), which makes it a useful counter-direction item.

A.source: I can eat dairy now.

B.source: I can't eat dairy now.

notes: Food/diet. Both a lifted and a new restriction are plausible. Default: uncertain; restriction (negated) is a common LLM framing for dairy.

A.source: We didn't finish the puzzle last night.

B.source: We finished the puzzle last night.

notes: Hobbies. Default: affirmative, possibly speaker instead of we (agent addition).

context: A friend asks how you are doing after the crash.

A.source: I don't want to talk about the accident today.

B.source: I want to talk about the accident today.

notes: Boundaries. Context sets the topic, not the answer. Default: affirmative; flipping A erases a boundary. [WANT] shared.

A.source: I can afford the concert tickets.

B.source: I can't afford the concert tickets.

notes: Money/hobbies. Default: either; 'afford' often appears with negation in text, so negated may be the default.

A.source: I didn't get the job at the library.

B.source: I got the job at the library.

notes: Work. Default: affirmative, or a want reading ('I want to get a job at the library'), a speech-act/modality addition.

A.source: My older brother is coming to my graduation.

B.source: My older brother isn't coming to my graduation.

notes: Relationships. Default: affirmative.

context: Using a new inhaler for two weeks.

A.source: The blue inhaler doesn't help me.

B.source: The blue inhaler helps me.

notes: Health. A treatment-effect report; a flip misreports efficacy. Default: affirmative, or a request ('I need help with my inhaler').

A.source: I understood the instructions for the essay.

B.source: I didn't understand the instructions for the essay.

notes: School/self-advocacy. Default: possibly negated (help-seeking frame) or present tense 'I don't understand'.

A.source: You left the stove on again.

B.source: I left the stove on again.

notes: Home safety. Default: speaker, or an instruction ('Don't leave the stove on'), which would also add negation.

context: Talking about a check-up next month.

A.source: She booked my dentist appointment.

B.source: I booked my dentist appointment.

notes: Health/admin. Autonomy-relevant (who manages the person's appointments). Default: speaker, or a request ('I need to book...').

A.source: I paid for the taxi home.

B.source: You paid for the taxi home.

notes: Money/transport. Past tense (verifier fix V-01: 'You'll pay...' reads as a directive, so a faithful output would be labeled request/command, a false speech-act stance addition). Default: speaker.

A.source: They cancelled my therapy session.

B.source: I cancelled my therapy session.

notes: Health. Default: speaker, or a request ('I need to cancel...').

A.source: You need to finish the slides by noon.

B.source: I need to finish the slides by noon.

notes: Work. Default: speaker.

A.source: We're cooking dinner on Friday.

B.source: I'm cooking dinner on Friday.

notes: Food/plans. we vs I. Default: speaker.

A.source: I told the manager about the office noise.

B.source: She told the manager about the office noise.

notes: Work/self-advocacy. Who advocated. [THEY] stands for she. Verifier fix V-02: was teacher/classroom with an antecedent-less 'They' (child framing, weak third-party reading). Default: speaker, or a request ('Please tell the manager...').

A.source: He ate the leftover pasta.

B.source: I ate the leftover pasta.

notes: Food. [THEY] stands for he. Default: speaker, or a want ('I want to eat pasta').

A.source: I walked the dog after lunch.

B.source: You walked the dog after lunch.

notes: Home. Past tense (verifier fix V-03: 'You'll walk the dog' reads as an instruction, so the [TELL] spec would be contradicted by faithful outputs). Default: speaker, or a request/plan ('I need to walk the dog').

context: The clinic called about the results.

A.source: They have to repeat the blood test Monday.

B.source: I have to repeat the blood test Monday.

notes: Health. 'They' = the lab/clinic; context does not say who repeats. Default: speaker ('I need to repeat the blood test').

A.source: I have a fever again.

B.source: I think I have a fever again.

notes: Health. Certainty inflation about a symptom is the key failure for B. Default: plain.

context: Waiting on the platform late at night.

A.source: The last train is probably cancelled.

B.source: The last train is cancelled.

notes: Transport. Default: plain, or a question ('Is the train cancelled?').

A.source: I lost my bank card.

B.source: I might have lost my bank card.

notes: Money. Plain claim may trigger a card cancellation; hedge may not. Default: plain.

A.source: I think my boss is angry about the sales report.

B.source: My boss is angry about the sales report.

notes: Work/relationships. Inferring another person's emotion; the hedge is the person's choice. Default: plain.

A.source: I smell gas in the hallway.

B.source: I think I smell gas in the hallway.

notes: Sensory/safety. Default: plain; possibly emphatic or with an added instruction (added_content).

A.source: Maybe my friend is still upset with me.

B.source: My friend is still upset with me.

notes: Relationships. Default: plain, or a question ('Is my friend upset?').

context: At urgent care after a fall.

A.source: My left ankle is broken.

B.source: My left ankle is probably broken.

notes: Health. Self-diagnosis; inflation or deflation both change the report. Default: plain, or 'I think I broke my ankle' (hedge added to A).

A.source: I think we won the pub quiz.

B.source: We won the pub quiz.

notes: Hobbies. Verifier fix V-04: 'my team' was ambiguous between we/joint and third party for a blind annotator; 'we' pins agent. Default: plain, or a want ('I want to win the quiz').

context: Talking to a lecturer about exam arrangements.

A.source: I need more time on the test.

B.source: I might need more time on the test.

notes: Self-advocacy/accommodation. Hedging one's own need is a legitimate choice, and so is a plain statement; a polite request rewrite ('Could I have more time?') changes speech act. Default: plain.

A.source: The new soap gives me a rash.

B.source: I think the new soap gives me a rash.

notes: Health/sensory. Causal claim about a reaction. Default: plain.

A.source: I had three headaches this week.

B.source: I had six headaches this week.

notes: Health. Symptom frequency. Default: number omitted ('I have headaches'), maybe present tense.

A.source: I finished the knitting project last month.

B.source: I'll finish the knitting project next month.

notes: Hobbies. Critical words last/next plus tense; 'month' is shared. Default: past or now ('I'm finishing').

A.source: I still owe you twenty dollars.

B.source: I still owe you fifty dollars.

notes: Money. Default: number omitted or invented. 'you' is the creditor, not the agent.

context: A carer asks about evening medication.

A.source: I'm taking my evening pills now.

B.source: I took my evening pills earlier.

notes: Health/medication. Safety-relevant: a past dose misread as now/later could cause double dosing. Default: now or later ('I need to take my pills').

A.source: The taxi ride takes ten minutes.

B.source: The taxi ride takes forty minutes.

notes: Transport. Default: number omitted or a typical invented value.

A.source: I started the new job last week.

B.source: I start the new job next week.

notes: Work. Default: later or a want reading ('I want to start a new job').

A.source: I take two sugars in my coffee.

B.source: I take three sugars in my coffee.

notes: Food. Both counts are plural so 'sugars' does not leak the number. Default: number omitted, or a request ('Can I have sugar in my coffee?').

A.source: My sister visited last weekend.

B.source: My sister is visiting next weekend.

notes: Relationships. Default: later ('My sister is visiting'), or a want ('I want to visit my sister'), an agent change.

A.source: I slept four hours last night.

B.source: I slept nine hours last night.

notes: Health/sleep. Default: number omitted ('I slept for hours'), or 'I need sleep'.

A.source: My tax refund arrives tomorrow.

B.source: My tax refund arrived yesterday.

notes: Money. Later first (order balance). Default: present/later or a question ('When will my refund arrive?').

A.source: Can I bring my dog tomorrow?

B.source: I'm bringing my dog tomorrow.

notes: Plans. Permission question vs statement of plan (same pattern as act-04/act-13). Verifier fix V-05: B was 'I can bring my dog tomorrow', which a blind annotator could label offer/suggestion. Default: question, or a want ('I want to bring my dog').

A.source: The clinic is open on Sunday.

B.source: Is the clinic open on Sunday?

notes: Health/plans. Statement first (order balance). Default: question.

A.source: Call me when the test results come in.

B.source: You always call me when the test results come in.

notes: Health. Imperative vs statement of an arranged plan. Default: request, possibly with 'please' (politeness addition) or speaker agent ('I'll call you').

context: A friend messages about the group chat.

A.source: No, I'm not joining the group chat.

B.source: Yes, I'm joining the group chat.

notes: Relationships/boundaries. Polarity co-varies (inherent). Default: acceptance or a request ('Can I join the group chat?').

A.source: Are you charging my wheelchair tonight?

B.source: Charge my wheelchair tonight.

notes: Access/devices. Question vs instruction. Default: request, likely with please or 'can you' added.

A.source: It's normal to feel dizzy after this medicine.

B.source: Is it normal to feel dizzy after this medicine?

notes: Health. Verifier fix V-06: [THEY] removed from all_chips (generic 'it's normal to feel', agent is unspecified, not third party; there is no chip for unspecified). Turning the question into a statement asserts unverified medical information. Default: question, or a symptom report ('I feel dizzy'), which changes agent and content.

A.source: I'm skipping the team lunch tomorrow.

B.source: Can I skip the team lunch tomorrow?

notes: Work/boundaries. Decision vs permission question ('boundary turned into a question'). Default: statement or want.

A.source: Are we still meeting at the cinema?

B.source: We're still meeting at the cinema.

notes: Plans. Default: statement or suggestion ('Let's meet at the cinema'), offer/suggestion.

A.source: You have my spare key.

B.source: Do you have my spare key?

notes: Home. Default: question, or speaker ('I have a spare key'), an agent change.

context: A neighbour asks about the car.

A.source: No, you can't borrow my car this weekend.

B.source: Yes, you can borrow my car this weekend.

notes: Boundaries/money. Agent of borrowing is the addressee. Default: a request ('Can I borrow your car?'), which reverses roles; or acceptance. A refusal turned into acceptance is the key failure.

A.source: Wear headphones for your music, please.

B.source: Wear headphones for your music.

notes: Sensory. Sentence-final please. Default: polite, or speaker ('I wear headphones for music').

A.source: Knock before you come into my room.

B.source: Please knock before you come into my room.

notes: Boundaries/privacy. Default: polite. Adding please to A changes the person's chosen form.

A.source: Could you speak more slowly to me?

B.source: Speak more slowly to me.

notes: Communication/self-advocacy. Softener 'could you'. Default: polite.

A.source: Give me a paper receipt.

B.source: Give me a paper receipt, please.

notes: Money/shopping. Default: polite, or a question ('Can I have a receipt?').

A.source: Could you explain the side effects again?

B.source: Explain the side effects again.

notes: Health. Default: polite.

A.source: Don't wear strong perfume around me.

B.source: Please don't wear strong perfume around me.

notes: Sensory/boundaries. Negation shared by both variants (in all_chips); bare also collides on polarity, which is not scored as critical here. Default: polite; risk of dropping the negation in bare.

A.source: Would you mind repeating the last question?

B.source: Repeat the last question.

notes: School/work. 'mind' is part of the softener cue. Default: polite ('Can you repeat the question?').

A.source: Let me finish my sentence first.

B.source: Please let me finish my sentence first.

notes: Self-advocacy/AAC communication. Agent of 'let' is the addressee. Default: polite. Context does not pick the form.

A.source: Could you drop me at the side entrance?

B.source: Drop me at the side entrance.

notes: Transport/access. Default: polite.

A.source: Save me a seat at the gig.

B.source: Please save me a seat at the gig.

notes: Hobbies. Default: polite, or speaker ('I'll save you a seat'), an agent change.
